newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares stabilise, end with firm bias.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares stabilise, end with firm bias.

text.p: * NZ shares stabilise to end with firmer bias, off high
* Market consolidates on low volume
* Fletcher Energy puts on solid gain
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
324 nil * NZSC cap index +13.37 at 4,762.55
357 -3 * Volume NZ$40 million. Futures +6 at 1,164
722 +7 * Other movers - +7 -8
New Zealand shares ended with a firm bias on Wednesday but off their earlier highs after an unconvincing follow-through from Wall Street's strong finish.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 6.96 points up 2,301.44, off its earlier high of 2,307.75, on turnover worth just NZ$40 million.

Fletcher Energy was exhibiting strength, firming seven cents to NZ$3.81, possibly in reaction to news on Tuesday that oil production in the September quarter was 11.0 percent up on the same period a year ago.
Air New Zealand was also strong, particularly the rights to the B shares, which gained 12 to NZ$1.47.
Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities said it had been disappointing not to see a stronger reaction to the Dow's 34.29-point gain.
"The tone struggled to be all that positive. It's still consolidating after the big run that it's had," he said.
Fletcher Paper was off four at NZ$2.58 on continuing earnings concerns in the depressed pulp and paper industry.
Telecom gained seven to NZ$7.22, off its high for the day of $7.24 and still a far cry from its recent record of $7.60.
Port of Tauranga, after a strong performance over the month, was down eight at NZ$2.37 on light turnover.
-- James Gray (64 9 302 1253
